definitions.explanation: The prolonged cry of a wolf, dog, or similar animal, especially one that carries over a distance.
Figuratively, complaints or threats made from a safe distance by someone who lacks the courage to confront directly. Similar to "barking from afar" in English.

examples.japanese: ⟦{狼|おおかみ}→狼：04334_ookami⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{聞|き}こえた→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧。
examples.english: I heard the howling of wolves.

examples.japanese: ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦サイレン→サイレン：26994_sairen⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{合|あ}わせて→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧。
examples.english: The dog started howling along with the siren.

examples.japanese: ⟦{満月|まんげつ}→満月：17598_mangetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧たち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{響|ひび}いていた→響く：00099_hibiku⟧。
examples.english: On the night of the full moon, the howling of dogs echoed through the air.

examples.japanese: ⟦{負|ま}けた→負ける：01134_makeru⟧⟦{相手|あいて}→相手：01677_aite⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}えだ。
examples.english: That's just sour grapes from the loser.

examples.japanese: ⟦ネット→ネット：05279_netto⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{批判|ひはん}→批判：03580_hihan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{所詮|しょせん}→所詮：10920_shosen⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧すぎない。
examples.english: Criticism on the internet is nothing more than empty barking.

examples.japanese: ⟦{本人|ほんにん}→本人：03627_honnin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何|なに}も→何も：03874_nanimo⟧⟦{言|い}えない→言う：00515_iu⟧くせ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、⟦{陰|かげ}→陰：14593_kage⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He can't say anything to the person's face, yet he keeps barking behind their back.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{遠|とお}い→遠い：00529_tooi⟧ (far, distant) and ⟦{吠|ほ}える→吠える：02415_hoeru⟧ (to bark, to howl). The え ending is the noun form of the verb.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遠吠|とおぼ}え⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to howl)
- ⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え (a dog's howling — also figuratively: impotent threats)
- ⟦{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}→負け犬：14255_makeinu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え (the howl of a losing dog — sour grapes)

The figurative sense (sense 2) comes from the image of a weak dog that howls from a safe distance rather than confronting an opponent directly. ⟦{負|ま}け{犬|いぬ}→負け犬：14255_makeinu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{遠吠|とおぼ}え is a well-known proverb meaning complaints or boasts from someone who has already lost.
